name: Commander's Commendation Award (full-size medal body)
size_basis: Body width 1.375 in = the standard ribbon width for this size (1 3/8 in full, 5/8 in miniature; DoDM 1348.33 as relayed by the coordination chat, not verified locally); proportions from the McChord rasters (disc = ribbon width); CAPR 39-3 gives no medal dimensions. Height is the constructed body plus suspension ring.

ribbon_ref.note: medal body only; the ribbon asset supplies the stripes and devices. ribbon_attach is where the ribbon meets the suspension loop.

source: Designed and measured from the Vanguard photograph commander-commendation.jpeg (reference only): disc, rim, lettering, emblem, bail and ring are parametric shapes in inches, the same model as the miniature drawn at 2.2x (design/commendation.js). Previously constructed from the McChord rasters.

fit.metric: same model as the miniature body, which is gated against the photograph (silhouette IoU, landmarks within 0.02 in, edge recall)
fit.note: Shape-built art at 2.2x, upright; ring and bail are cut open at the box top where the box cuts them.

measured.photo: commander-commendation.jpeg (Vanguard photograph, 600 x 600 px, reference only)

frame.note: body width 0.625 in (the spec width) sets the scale; every length below is inches in the medal frame (origin = disc centre, +y down, UPRIGHT: the photograph is rotated by the measured hang angle into this frame)

measured.hang_angle_note: measured from the bail axis against the disc centre in the photograph (frame.js); the drawing hangs upright (bail and disc axis vertical)
not_measurable: The matte stippled field (the dots, pits and speckle of the textured ground inside and outside the C) is texture: it is drawn as one flat ground tone, not as dots.

Mirror reflections in the polished surfaces (the dark faces of the C and of the triangle, the white and blue glints on the bail and the base bar) are drawn as flat tones: dark face 26 and 18, bright bevels 215.
The blades' matte interior carries a fine engraved pattern that the photograph barely resolves: drawn as one flat tone.

The rim: the photograph shows a bright outer lip, a thin groove and a raised ridge; their radii (0.303 to 0.3125, 0.298 to 0.302, 0.2865 to 0.2985 in) are read from radial profiles on the lit left side.

The right and lower bevels of the C are dim in the photograph (the light comes from the upper left); their radii and the two slanted end cuts are fitted from the lit left side and from the end views, the end-cut angles are good to about 2 degrees.
The suspension ring is hidden by the ribbon: its centre and radius (0.145 in outer) are fitted to the visible lower arcs; the bail is a polished barrel whose glints are not drawn.
The triangle is not exactly symmetric in the photograph (side bars 31.7 and 29.3 degrees off vertical, apex 0.008 in right of the base middle): the measured corners are used as they are.
This photograph is a miniature (the disc is 0.625 in); no lettering exists on this medal face.
